A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CABLE and its length-extrapolation experiments. All text, equations, tables, and figures are readable across v1's 11 pages and v2's 13 pages, including v2's Appendix A. v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 report original perplexity results, unseen-data evaluations, runtime and memory measurements, and ablation studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original language-model experiments, BERT retrieval results in Table 2, and additional training-loss curves and perplexity results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: v1 generates token biases using one linear layer and negative Softplus. v2 introduces ReLU bias increments and a second linear/Softplus branch producing token-dependent multiplicative weights (Section 3, Equations 2–7). This substantially changes the bias construction. CABLE NW is v2's unweighted variant, not an exact renaming of v1's method.

E1.justification: FineWeb-Edu and WikiText-103 next-token prediction remain, while v2 adds BERT masked-language-model pretraining, MS-MARCO retrieval fine-tuning, and English MLDR long-document retrieval evaluation. v1's reported unseen-data evaluation, including HellaSwag and WikiText-2, is removed rather than relocated.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Sinusoidal, RoPE, T5-bias, and ALiBi. v2 additionally evaluates Learnable absolute embeddings, logarithmic Kerple, and Fire in language-model comparisons and the runtime figure. Kerple and Fire were previously discussed without corresponding experimental comparisons. The new retrieval comparison evaluates ALiBi, RoPE, Learnable, and Sinusoidal against CABLE.

E3.justification: The reported FineWeb-Edu training/evaluation split changes from 9B/1B to 9.9B/0.1B tokens, and WikiText-103 Tiny training changes from 5k to 9k steps. Language-model training is consolidated at length 1024, and maximum evaluation length changes from 16,384 to 15,360. Additional model-size conditions and a new BERT pretraining/fine-tuning protocol with nDCG@10 retrieval evaluation substantially expand the experimental design.

E4.justification: v2 adds CABLE-versus-CABLE-NW comparisons testing learned weights and Appendix A.1 analyses of BERT training convergence. It removes v1's training-length sweep and learned-bias visualizations (Figures 5, 7, and 8). The kernelization study remains, but v2 Figure 4 covers training length 1024 rather than both 512 and 1024 in v1 Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2's additional tables and training curves retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Language-model and runtime results are extensively revised. For example, v1 reports WikiText-103 perplexity 21.97 at length 16,384, whereas v2 Table 1 reports 20.33 at 15,360 under changed method and training conditions; this is not a same-setting gain. New retrieval results include CABLE 25.10 versus ALiBi 23.44 nDCG@10 at 16,384 tokens. Appendix Tables 3–4 add model-specific results, while v1's unseen-data results are removed.

T1.justification: Formal revisions concern the bias definition and its weighted ALiBi special case. Section 5.4 also changes the kernel from -log(1/(b^2+1)) to -log(b^2+1), a substantive sign reversal. These are localized mathematical revisions; neither version supplies theorems, proofs, or formal extrapolation guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the work from decoder language modeling to include BERT long-context retrieval. v1's headline comparison claiming 0.65 lower perplexity and 48% lower memory when training at length 512 instead of 1024 is removed. v2 instead emphasizes performance across positional-encoding comparators, encoder applicability, and relatively fast inference.

C2.justification: The central adaptive-bias and kernel-locality interpretations remain. v2 adds an interpretation of the learned-weight ablation and substantive qualifications: occasional short-context underperformance against RoPE, training overhead, dependence on training positional patterns, potential costs above 100K tokens, and unresolved theoretical behavior. The above-100K discussion identifies an untested concern, not an experimental finding.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new BERT pipeline, including bert-base-uncased, four H100 GPUs, Adam at 1e-4, 14k pretraining steps, and 1.25M fine-tuning samples with mined hard negatives using sentence-transformers. It also revises language-model hardware from two to eight H100 GPUs and supplies additional training budgets. Conversely, the runtime presentation loses v1's explicit sequence-length conditions. The code-access link remains substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands research positioning, adding FoX as concurrent related work and Barbero et al.'s critique of RoPE's distance-decay explanation. New encoder/retrieval literature supports the expanded scope. Discussions and citations concerning randomized and hybrid positional encodings, including Ruoss et al., He et al., and Tong Wu et al., are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and results narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Related work gains explicit NoPE/APE/RPE organization, the contribution list changes, and the results structure replaces the generalization section with bidirectional-model evaluation. A limitations discussion and Appendix A are added. GPT-3 terminology changes to GPT-2 while the stated decoder dimensions remain the same.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn around the weighted method, and extrapolation and runtime charts are redesigned with additional comparators. Extensive numerical tables replace much of the earlier plot-based language-model presentation. v1's training-length and bias-matrix figures disappear, while v2 adds a retrieval table, appendix result tables, and two training-loss plots.

improvement.justification: Evaluating Fire and Kerple and explicitly comparing CABLE with CABLE NW strengthen empirical support and component attribution; the BERT retrieval experiment also tests broader applicability. The net gain is limited by removing v1's generalization and training-length analyses while retaining the conclusion's claim about outperforming a baseline trained at length 8192. Reporting inconsistencies also remain: Appendix A.2 claims consistent superiority, although Table 3 reports ALiBi 26.80 versus CABLE 26.97 for GPT-Tiny at length 8192.
